product.category: Windows-first read-only driver and hardware diagnostics workbench
product.summary: A Windows-first workbench for hardware inventory, driver-package inspection, integrity evidence and structured diagnostic reports; it does not install or modify drivers.
proof_points: Read-only Windows Plug and Play inventory.
Bounded INF, ZIP and UDRV package inspection without payload execution.
Evidence-linked reports and normalized device snapshots.
non_claims: OPlague does not install, update, remove or modify drivers.
Inspection results are not a guarantee of device compatibility or a certified driver recommendation.
Market demand, paid conversion and profitability are not established.

audiences.audience: IT support technicians and system administrators
audiences.need: Inspect hardware and driver packages while retaining a clear evidence trail.
audiences.value: A read-only workflow for inventory, package review and diagnostic reporting.

audiences.need: Understand device identity and package metadata before separate administrative action.
audiences.value: Structured evidence without automated installation or destructive changes.

audiences.audience: Driver packagers and hardware QA teams
audiences.need: Review package structure, hashes and declared metadata under resource limits.
audiences.value: Bounded inspection and deterministic report composition.

positioning.statement: OPlague is a read-only Windows workbench for inspecting hardware identity and driver-package evidence before any separate maintenance action.
differentiators: Read-only device inventory with no driver installation or modification.
Bounded package inspection treats imported files as untrusted input.
Reports preserve evidence and distinguish exact matches from uncertain similarity.

brand.promise: Make hardware and driver-package inspection safer, clearer and evidence-led.

stages.name: Problem discovery
stages.success_criteria: Collect workflow evidence from IT support, repair and driver QA users.

stages.name: Message and documentation
stages.success_criteria: README and product documentation state the read-only boundary and inspection workflow.

stages.name: Distribution
stages.success_criteria: Windows desktop packaging and the public source/release workflow are documented.

stages.name: User validation
stages.success_criteria: Validate the diagnostic workflow with representative, consented operator feedback.

stages.name: Retention and support
stages.success_criteria: Define supported Windows versions, package-format policy and issue triage.

channels.name: GitHub repository and Windows release information
channels.purpose: Explain read-only capabilities, supported package inputs and safety boundaries.
channels.guardrail: Never advertise automated driver updates or universal compatibility.

channels.name: Technical walkthroughs
channels.purpose: Demonstrate inventory, package inspection and evidence reports.
channels.guardrail: Use sanitized examples; do not expose device identifiers or personal machine data.

channels.name: IT support and repair communities
channels.purpose: Collect real operator workflows and usability feedback.
channels.guardrail: No unsupported repair guarantees or aggressive promotion.

channels.name: Release notes and compatibility matrix
channels.purpose: Make supported Windows versions and tested formats discoverable.
channels.guardrail: List exact tested versions and keep unknown combinations explicit.

market_validation.notes: No measured customer demand or workflow adoption is asserted.

pricing.notes: No paid tier, subscription or willingness-to-pay assumption is published.

unit_economics.notes: Packaging, maintenance and support costs require measurement.

licensing.notes: Review application license, PowerShell usage, dependencies and third-party notices.

support.notes: Define Windows support policy, triage and maintenance lifecycle.

distribution.notes: The repository contains a Windows desktop build/release path; each release artifact must be verified individually.

metrics.name: First completed inspection
metrics.definition: Share of evaluators who complete an inventory or package-review workflow.
metrics.source: Consent-based usability feedback or documented support reports.
metrics.privacy_note: Do not collect machine identifiers through hidden telemetry.

metrics.name: Evidence completeness
metrics.definition: Share of reports containing required source references and inspection metadata.
metrics.privacy_note: Do not treat completeness as proof of compatibility.

metrics.name: Support resolution
metrics.definition: Time from reproducible issue to verified fix or documented limitation.
metrics.source: Public issue history and release notes.
metrics.privacy_note: Sanitize logs and attachments before publication.

governance.claims: Describe OPlague as read-only. Never claim to install, update, repair or certify drivers; qualify match and compatibility statements.
governance.promotion: Demonstrate safe inspection and evidence provenance, not automatic remediation or guaranteed fixes.
governance.privacy: Sanitize screenshots, reports and examples; do not publish serial numbers, hostnames or personal device inventories.
governance.rights: Review dependency licenses and third-party notices before packaging or redistribution.
